RESPONSE_TO: CC2  
Confirmed. I traced the path and agree your lock objection is real and load-bearing. `_reconciliation_gate()` documents a lock invariant but returns only `(verdicts, confidences)`, so no lock state survives. In `run_immune_pipeline()`, the autoimmune override unconditionally resets `filtered`/`rejected`, which necessarily discards any supposedly immutable rejection state. This is not just a doc/code drift; it nullifies the gate’s stated safety property. I am not repeating it as a new finding because it is already established.

@Gemini: Your D005 adds monotonic `record_count`, which is necessary, but I think `_verify_epoch()` also fails to validate `epoch_index` continuity/type. A malformed epoch list with duplicate or non-integer `epoch_index` values would still pass root verification. If you have evidence this was already covered elsewhere, point me to it.

@Codex: Your R12 findings on post-immune persistence are directionally right. I found a narrower persistence-layer bug in `insect_brain.py`: immune output is attached only to in-memory `RoundRecord` and is never checkpointed nor written to any sibling JSON artifact, so restart destroys it even before audit questions arise.

    def build_inclusion_proof(self, index: int, epoch_index: Optional[int] = None) -> dict:
        """Build an RFC 9162 inclusion proof for the record at `index` within a sealed epoch."""
        if not (0 <= index < len(self._records)):
            raise IndexError(
                f"Index {index} out of range [0, {len(self._records)})"
            )
        if not self._epochs:
            raise ValueError("Cannot build inclusion proof without a sealed epoch")
        if epoch_index is None:
            epoch = self._epochs[-1]
        else:
            if not (0 <= epoch_index < len(self._epochs)):
                raise IndexError(
                    f"Epoch index {epoch_index} out of range [0, {len(self._epochs)})"
                )
            epoch = self._epochs[epoch_index]
        record_count = int(epoch["record_count"])
        if index >= record_count:
            raise IndexError(
                f"Record index {index} not included in epoch {epoch['epoch_index']} with record_count={record_count}"
            )
        leaves = [_digest_bytes(r["chain_hash"]) for r in self._records[:record_count]]
        proof_steps = rfc9162_inclusion_proof(leaves, index)
        return {
            "epoch_index": epoch["epoch_index"],
            "record_count": record_count,
            "index": index,
            "chain_hash": self._records[index]["chain_hash"],
